MFA No. 370 of 2019

THIS MFA IS FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 24/07/2018, PASSED IN MVC NO.133/2014, ON THE FILE OF THE SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND JMFC., AND MACT, PAVAGADA, AWARDING COMPENSATION OF RS.8,92,104/- WITH INTEREST AT THE RATE OF 6% P.A., FROM THE DATE OF THE CLAIM PETITION UNTIL REALIZATION OF THE ENTIRE AWARD AMOUNT.

THIS APPEAL HAVING BEEN HEARD AND RESERVED FOR JUDGMENT AND COMING ON FOR PRONOUNCEMENT OF JUDGMENT THIS DAY THROUGH VIDEO CONFERENING AT KALABURGI, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal by the Insurance Company is directed against the judgment and award dated 24/07/2018, passed in MVC No.133/2014, by the learned Senior Civil Judge and JMFC and MACT,
Pavagada, whereby, a sum of Rs.8,92,104/- has been awarded as compensation together with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition until realization on account of the death of one V.Manjunatha in the road traffic accident.

2. It is the case of the petitioner that, on 02.06.2013 at about 03.10 p.m., while the petitioner and her husband V.Manjunatha were returning in their motorcycle bearing KA-06- EK-9851 from Ananthapuram to Pavagada after attending a function in their relatives house along with their grandsons namely Karthik (7 years) and Venkatesh @ Venki (2 years) on NC: 2023:KHC:40581 NH-44 road, near Dadalur Village, Kanaganaalli mandal, the driver of Indica Vista car bearing registration No.AP-21-AP-0854 came with a high speed and in rash and negligent manner from opposite direction and dashed to their motorcycle bearing KA-06- EK-9851 and caused the accident.
As a result the petitioner, her husband and their grandsons fell down and sustained bleeding injuries.
Immediately, they were shifted to Government Hospital in 108 Ambulance vehicle and her husband ultimately died in the said Government Hospital.
3. The death of her husband V.Manjunatha was due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the Tata Indica Vista car bearing registration No.AP-21-AP-0854 which belong to respondent No.1.

Petitioner is the sole dependent of the deceased, who was aged 50 years at the time of accident,
working as Tailor and getting monthly income Rs.15,000/- from his tailoring works and due to his untimely death, she has suffered shock, mental agony, and loss of dependency.
It was further contended that the said car had been insured by the respondent No.2 as per the policy No.015202004000 valid from 20.07.2012 to 19.07.2013.

Hence, the respondent Nos.1 and 2 NC:
2023:KHC:40581 are jointly and severely liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner.

sentences.text: In response to the notice issued by the Tribunal, the respondents appeared through their counsels and respondent No.2 filed its written statement denying the petition averments and contending that, the petition is false, vexatious and the same is not maintainable in law or on facts of the case and that the offending vehicle is no way concerned with the accident.
It was further contended that compensation claimed is exorbitant and untenable and prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. On the basis of the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed appropriate issues and petitioner examined herself as PW.1 and examined one witness as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P1 to P17.
Respondents have not produced any oral or documentary evidence.

6. After hearing the learned counsel for both the sides, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.8,92,104/- as compensation under the following heads and directed the insurance company to deposit the same:
NC: 2023:KHC:40581 AMOUNT PARTICULARS (IN RS.)

Total loss of estate 8,32,104/-
 Towards funeral expenses and 20,000/-
 transportation of dead body  Towards loss of love and affection 30,000/-
 and mental agony

Towards loss of consortium 10,000/-
 TOTAL 8,92,104/-
7. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the Insurance Company has approached this court in appeal.
8. On issuance of notice, respondent No.1 appeared through his counsel before this Court and despite service of notice, respondent No.2 did not appear.
On admitting the appeal, the Tribunal records have been secured.

9. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for appellant-Insurance Company and learned counsel for respondent No.1 and perused the Tribunal records.
10.
The learned counsel appearing for the appellant/Insurance Company contended that there were violations of terms and conditions of policy.
It is contended that the deceased was carrying three pillion riders and was riding the two wheeler without helmet contrary to the rules framed under NC: 2023:KHC:40581 the MV act.
It is alleged that he was not having any valid DL which constituted contributory negligence.
It was contended that the Tribunal has observed that the driver of the Tata Indica car was convicted but however, he had been acquitted by the Criminal Court.
He also contended that the Tribunal has erred in holding the income of the deceased at Rs.8,000/- per month in the absence of any cogent evidence.

He also submitted that the age of the deceased is 63 years but even then the Tribunal has Legal Cell, Tata Aig General Insurance ... vs Smt. V. Narayanamma on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100467445/
3 accepted as 50 years in ascertaining the multiplier.

entities.text: Legal Cell, Tata Aig General Insurance ... vs Smt. V. Narayanamma
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He also contended that the major son and married daughters were not the dependant and therefore, the Tribunal should have taken the personal expenses at 50%.
Hence, it is contended that the approach of the Tribunal was not proper and the appeal deserves to be allowed.
11. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the claimant has contended that there was no evidence lead by the insurer to show that there was any contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.
It is contended that carrying petitioner and two minor children as pillion riders cannot be a ground to hold that there was contributory negligence.
There was no overt NC: 2023:KHC:40581 act which amounted to contributory negligence and there is no evidence to show that the deceased was not wearing a helmet.
He submitted that the age of the deceased was properly considered by the Tribunal and the income has been assessed at Rs.8,000/- per month based on his avocation, which is just and proper.

12. In this regard, he has placed reliance on the decision in the case of KARNATAKA STATE ROAD TRANSPORT CORPORATION Vs. BELLAPPA1 and MEERA DEVI AND ANOTHER VS.
HIMACHAL PRADESH ROAD TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND OTHERS2.
13.

entities.text:
KARNATAKA STATE ROAD TRANSPORT CORPORATION Vs. BELLAPPA1 and MEERA DEVI AND ANOTHER VS.
HIMACHAL PRADESH ROAD TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND OTHERS2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A perusal of the FIR at Ex.P1 and other Police papers at Exs.P2 to P9 and P11 and P12 do not show anywhere that the deceased was not wearing a helmet.

The judgment of the Criminal Court wherein, the driver of the Tata Indica car was acquitted produced at Ex.P13 also does not show that the deceased Manjunath was not wearing a helmet at the time of the accident.

The contentions of the Insurance Company that the ILR 2017 KAR 1292 (2014) 4 SCC 511 NC: 2023:KHC:40581 deceased was not wearing a helmet appears to be speculative as the deceased had sustained head injury.
Therefore, the contention of the learned counsel for the appellant that the deceased was not wearing a helmet, is bereft of any acceptable evidence.
The cross-examination of PW.1 show that she has specifically denied the suggestion that the deceased was not wearing a helmet.
Hence, this argument has to be rejected.
14. The second ground of the appellant is that there were three pillion riders which violated the provisions of Motor Vehicles Rules.
The decision in the case of MEERA DEVI AND ANOTHER (Supra) lays down at paragraph No.10 as below:
"10. To prove the contributory negligence, there must be cogent evidence.
In the instant case, there is no specific evidence to prove that the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the deceased Scooterist.
In the absence of any cogent evidence to prove the plea of contributory negligence, the said doctrine of common law cannot be applied in the present case.

We are, thus, of the view that the reasoning given by the High Court has no basis and the compensation awarded by the Tribunal was just and reasonable in the facts and circumstances of the case."
Legal Cell, Tata Aig General Insurance ... vs Smt. V. Narayanamma on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100467445/
4 15.

It is evident that non-possession of the driving license, underage of the injured/deceased,
violation of certain NC: 2023:KHC:40581 rules by themselves cannot be a ground to hold that there was contributory negligence.
This view was also taken by this Court in umpteen number of decisions.

The decision in the case of BELLAPPA (Supra) also specifically observes as below:
"Excess passengers carried in a vehicle by itself would not be construed as breach on the part of the owner/insured of
the vehicle.-Merely
because the deceased was riding motorcycle with two persons on the vehicle though amounts to contravention of Section 128 of the Act, it does not amount to negligent act on the part of the deceased.

The rider riding the vehicle, if it is demonstrated lost control of the vehicle, he was not able to balance the vehicle or because of such contravention he dashed against the vehicle which resulted in accident.
then the question of extent of breach of duty resulted in negligence would be analysed.
Even assuming that the injured was a pillion itself would not disentitle the claimant from claiming compensation.

Secondly,
violation of Section 128 of the Act and relevant rules would be amenable to punitive action but that itself would not result in breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy, the Corporation cannot escape the liability to pay the compensation."
16.

In that view of the matter, unless it is established that the deceased was riding the motorcycle with negligence, it cannot be said that non-compliance of certain rules and regulations would ipsofacto constitute negligence.

Hence, the very fact that there were two minors, who were grandchildren of - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:40581 the deceased and the petitioner were also the pillion riders cannot be a ground to hold there was contributory negligence.
17. The third ground raised is with regard the age of the deceased.
The Aadhar Card of the deceased produced at Ex.P16 shows the year of birth to be 1950.
The Voters ID card produced at Ex.P15 shows that his date of birth was 01.02.1956.

The Tribunal has accepted the age as mentioned in the PM report, which is 50 years and though observes the proper multiplier would be '14', while calculating adopts the multiplier of '13'.
18.
Obviously, the accident had occurred on 02.06.2013.

The age as mentioned in Aadhar Card would be more reliable as it involves verification of the documents relied at the time of the enrolment, whereas, the Voters Card would not involve such verification of other acceptable documents.
Therefore, the age as per the Aadhar Card would be 63 years.

Appropriate multiplier for the age of 63 would be '7'.
19.
The Tribunal has taken the income of the deceased at Rs.8,000/- per month.

It is based on an assessment of Ex.P10 Legal Cell, Tata Aig General Insurance ... vs Smt. V. Narayanamma on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100467445/
5 - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:40581 to show that he was a Tailor.

entities.text: Ex.P10 Legal Cell, Tata Aig General Insurance ... vs Smt. V. Narayanamma
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I do not find any reason to differ with the said income assessed by the Tribunal.
20. The deceased is survived by the petitioner and therefore, 1/3rd has to be deducted towards the 'personal expenses'.
I do not find any substance in the argument of the learned counsel for the appellant, when there is dependent, 50% personal expenses should has been considered by the Tribunal.
This argument is absurd and untenable and bereft of any acceptable reason.

Hence, 'loss of dependency' is calculated as Rs.8,000 X 12 X 7 X 2/3 = Rs.4,48,000/-.
21.

So far as other heads of compensation is concerned, in view of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS3, there shall be an enhancement of 10% for every three years and therefore, compensation under the head of 'loss of consortium' is held to be Rs.48,400/- and the compensation under the head of 'loss of estate and funeral expenses' are held to be at Rs.18,150/- each.

entities.text: NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, the petitioner is entitled for the modified compensation under different heads as below:
AMOUNT PARTICULARS (IN RS.)

Loss of dependency 4,48,000/-
 Loss of consortium 48,400/-
 Loss of estate 18,150/-
 Funeral expenses 18,150/-
 TOTAL 5,32,700/-
23.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,32,700/- instead of Rs.8,92,104/- together with interest at the rate of 6% per annum and therefore, the appeal by the Insurance Company deserves to be allowed in part.

Hence, the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal filed by the Insurance Company is allowed in part.
(ii) The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified by awarding a sum of Rs.5,32,700/- instead of Rs.8,92,104/- together with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization .
